ac_coverage.criterion: EvalChild takes its child EvalContext from the per-call collector, which keeps one context per depth and resets it for each child. A new unit test shows that sibling children at the same depth reuse one context and that every reset clears all per-child state.
The caller still owns the returned units slice. A new test shows that units returned for one child are not aliased or overwritten when a later sibling at the same depth is evaluated.
A doc comment next to EvalChild and the per-depth context stack states two rules: no keyword may keep its child context after EvalChild returns, and the caller owns the returned units slice.

In test binaries only, a reused child context is wiped (poisoned) as soon as EvalChild returns, so any later use fails loudly. A new test proves that a keyword which keeps its child context fails under this check. Production builds behave as without the check.

Any keyword found to need data from its child context after EvalChild returns keeps a fresh context, as today. Each such keyword is named in the story record and documented next to the code. No applicator, annotate or recording file is edited for this.
Per-call state (the context stack) is never shared between Validate calls. go test -race ./... is green, including a new concurrent-validation test that exercises reused child contexts.
All existing tests pass unchanged. None is removed or weakened. allocs_test.go and docs/benchmarks.md are not edited.

The #205 golden comparison test passes: CLI stdout, stderr and exit code are byte-identical to the committed v1.1 golden files in flag, basic, detailed and verbose. No golden file is regenerated or edited.

A new root-package file allocs_childctx_test.go holds this story's lowered allocation limits for the guarded scenarios. Each limit is the measured value plus about 10% headroom, with the measured value recorded next to it. The file reuses the helpers and race gating of allocs_test.go and allocs_race_on/off_test.go without editing them.

A new file docs/benchmarks/r3-206-childctx.md records the following: before medians (main after #205) and after medians from go test -bench -count=10 on the same machine (B/op, allocs/op, ns/op); the absolute values after the story; and a verdict for each target. Targets: Validate5_5MB at most 200 MB B/op combined (the 305 MB stand-alone target is noted as not measured); ValidateErrors drops by at least about 4.8 MB B/op; ValidateSmall drops by at least about 6,200 B/op. Timings are noted as noisy because they were taken during a parallel build, to be re-measured at Checkpoint 3.
If any target is missed, the numbers are recorded and the story is held for the operator's decision. It is never marked done silently.
Standard library only. go.mod is unchanged.

adr.summary: The change does what the story asks without changing behaviour. EvalChild now reuses one child context per depth from a per-call stack. reset replaces the whole struct, so nothing leaks between siblin

assumptions.text: Medians were computed by hand from the 10 runs. B/op and allocs/op barely vary, so the B/op medians are rounded to about 10 bytes.
The 'before' baseline is the worktree HEAD 079149b, which includes #205.
Timings were taken during a parallel build and are noisy; the operator re-measures at Checkpoint 3.
Validate5_5MB before is already about 269 MB, so the 200 MB combined target needs about a 69 MB drop from this story.
The collector struct is in annotate.go, which is outside this task's files, so childStack is a separate type. T3 will hold it per call and add a depth to EvalContext in registry.go.
reset sets units to nil rather than truncating. Units are still allocated only when a child reports a failure, as before, and the caller owns the slice.
Every current EvalChild caller uses only the returned (ok, units, err) and never touches the child context, so no keyword needs the fresh-context path. The list of fresh-context keywords is empty.
A hand-built EvalContext with no stack (nil stk) still gets a freshly allocated child, as before.
Importing the testing package for testing.Testing() into internal/keywords is acceptable, as the design chose. It only reads a flag and registers no test flags.
The poison test uses a hand-built root context with a stub evalNode as the retaining keyword. Real keywords never see their child context outside EvalChild.
internal/keywords/registry.go was edited because the call to poison has to sit in EvalChild; no other keyword file was touched.
Limits are measured values plus about 10%, rounded up: ValidateSmall 509 allocs (limit 560) and 23,216 B (25,600); Validate5_5MB 196,951,210 B (216,700,000); ValidateErrors 15,511,248 B (17,100,000).
Only bytes are guarded for the 5.5 MB and Errors scenarios, because the allocs_test.go count limits for them are unchanged by this story.
The measured values were taken on the current worktree code, which has T1-T4 in place.
Medians were computed by hand from the 10 runs of each benchmark; for an even count I averaged the two middle values.
The 'before' table was left as recorded by T1 and not re-measured.
